'''Related games''' are other card games connected to ''Star Wars'' CCG through Decipher, the ''Star Wars'' license, or shared designers and players.

Decipher's first major CCG was ''Star Trek: The Next Generation'' (1994), followed by ''Star Wars'' CCG (1995) and later titles including ''Austin Powers'', ''Young Jedi'', ''Jedi Knights'', ''The Lord of the Rings'' TCG, several youth-market licenses, the original-IP ''WARS'' TCG, and finally ''Fight Klub''.<ref name="wp-decipher">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decipher,_Inc. Decipher, Inc.], Wikipedia</ref><ref name="lotr-decipher">[https://wiki.lotrtcgpc.net/wiki/Decipher Decipher], LOTR-TCG Wiki</ref> See [[Decipher]] and [[Decipher after the Star Wars license]].

== Decipher Star Wars games ==
; [[Young Jedi]] (1999–2001)
: Decipher's ''Star Wars'' customizable card game based on ''The Phantom Menace'', separate from SWCCG. Eight sets came out between May 1999 and September 2001, from ''Menace of Darth Maul'' to ''Boonta Eve Podrace''.<ref name="yjcl">[http://www.decipher.com/youngjedi/cardlists/index.html Young Jedi Card Lists], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20021201080954/http://www.decipher.com/youngjedi/cardlists/index.html Internet Archive]</ref>
; [[Jedi Knights Trading Card Game]] (2001)
: Decipher's third ''Star Wars'' card game, set in the original trilogy, with computer-generated card art.<ref name="sfw">Lee Bates, [http://www.scifi.com/sfw/issue199/games.html Jedi Knights Trading Card Game (review)], ''Science Fiction Weekly'', SciFi.com (2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20071211183732/http://www.scifi.com/sfw/issue199/games.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="pyr">[http://www.sjgames.com/pyramid/sample.html?id=2388 Pyramid Review: Jedi Knights CCG], ''Pyramid'', Steve Jackson Games (17 August 2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20220110205654/http://www.sjgames.com/pyramid/sample.html?id=2388 Internet Archive]</ref> Decipher stopped publishing SWCCG, Young Jedi and Jedi Knights effective 31 December 2001.<ref name="ann">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/announcement122801.html The Star Wars Announcement], decipher.com (28 December 2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20020601152726/http://decipher.com/starwars/announcement122801.html Internet Archive]</ref>

; [[SWCCG 2nd Edition]] (unreleased)
: Decipher's July 2000 pitch for a 2001 reboot. Lucasfilm did not approve it.

== After the license moved ==
; [[Star Wars Trading Card Game]] (2002–)
: Wizards of the Coast's ''Star Wars'' card game, published from April 2002 under the license Lucasfilm moved from Decipher and designed by Richard Garfield. It used all-new mechanics and was not compatible with SWCCG.<ref name="wp-swtcg">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Trading_Card_Game Star Wars Trading Card Game], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260202232757/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Trading_Card_Game Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="icv2-2002">[https://icv2.com/articles/games/view/983/wizards-coast-gets-star-wars-ccg Wizards of the Coast Gets Star Wars CCG], ICv2 (1 January 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008201620/https://icv2.com/articles/games/view/983/wizards-coast-gets-star-wars-ccg Internet Archive]</ref>
; [[WARS TCG]] (2004–2005)
: Decipher's original science-fiction card game. It reused the SWCCG turn, Force-pile economy, location control and battle structure so Star Wars players could pick it up quickly. Its sets ran from ''Incursion'' (October 2004) to ''Nowhere to Hide'' (January 2005).<ref name="warsrules">[https://www.cardgamecollector.com/images/wars-tcg/WARS-TCG-Incursion-Rulebook.pdf WARS TCG Incursion Rulebook], Decipher, 2004</ref>

== Other Decipher games ==
; [[The Lord of the Rings Trading Card Game]] (2001–2007)
: Decipher's game based on Peter Jackson's films. It became Decipher's main game after the ''Star Wars'' license ended, and fans have kept it going since 2007.<ref name="pcdec">[https://wiki.lotrtcgpc.net/wiki/Decipher Decipher], LOTR-TCG Wiki (Player's Council). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008212029/https://wiki.lotrtcgpc.net/wiki/Decipher Internet Archive]</ref>
